minutes.headline: Commission heard that enforcing demolition by neglect means court, and agreed to ask Town Council about a fines option.
minutes.summary: The commission met with the building commissioner (by Zoom) about how the district bylaw's demolition-by-neglect provisions can actually be enforced. He said the only mechanism is court action approved by the select board, and suggested asking Town Council whether fines under a zoning-style enforcement section could be added for the district. The members also discussed a Town Hall chimney bid, the master plan steering committee, a draft owner brochure, and ideas for historic signs and a walking tour.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the 12 September meeting.
Motion to adjourn (motion text garbled; all in favor said I).

budget_items.topic: Freedom's Way National Heritage Area matching grant
budget_items.what_was_said: A reimbursable matching grant is available, accepted on a rolling basis; the chair is considering whether it could help a private owner of a significant property.
The one bid received was far above the amount appropriated at town meeting. Members worried the Ritter building and ramp work will also exceed budgets.

budget_items.topic: Fines under non-criminal enforcement for zoning violations
budget_items.what_was_said: The building commissioner described daily fines available under zoning enforcement that could be stayed if owners work on repairs.
Noted Lunenburg did not adopt the CPA after several tries; it was raised as a possible source of repair and walking-tour funds.

decisions.decision: The chair will find the Town Council schedule and arrange a meeting, which Brian and commission members may join, to ask whether fines can be tied to demolition-by-neglect enforcement.
The chair will ask the facilities manager to report on the chimney phase, noting the commission's conditional approval.
The chair will email a draft brochure for edits, aiming to print and mail it within the district before the end of the calendar year.
The January meeting may be devoted to reviewing the National Register nomination to identify resources for markers and signs.
The next meeting was set for 14 November.
The chair will email thoughts on the heritage grant and contact its executive director about the application timeline; discussion at the November meeting.
